items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 12 at 11:51AM PST until November 15 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet with sets to 8 to 9
feet at northwest facing beaches. High rip current risk.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 10 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides will be falling during this time, but
adjusted high tides may still be near 7 feet which could combine
with the high surf to result in localized beach erosion and
overflow into parking lots and boardwalks. Surf begins to wane
Sunday afternoon but may remain elevated for west-facing beaches
into Monday morning.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 12 at 12:04PM PST until November 14 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Seas 5 to 9 ft and west winds 20 to 25 knots will lead
to choppy seas and dangerous boating conditions.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican
Border and out to 10 nm and Waters from San Mateo Point to the
Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San
Clemente Island.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds in the outer coastal waters
with the highest seas near and south of San Clemente Island.
Seas and winds will begin to wane Saturday afternoon, but seas
may remain above 7 feet into early Sunday.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
